purpose: Isotretinoin is used to treat severe acne that has not gotten better with other treatments like antibiotics or creams. It is often the most powerful and effective option for stubborn, scarring acne. Most people see dramatic improvement or complete clearing of their acne after one course of treatment.
how_it_works: Isotretinoin works by dramatically shrinking the oil glands in your skin, which makes them produce much less oil. Since acne-causing bacteria thrive in oily environments, less oil means fewer breakouts. It also helps your skin cells shed more normally so pores are less likely to become clogged.
common_side_effects: Very dry lips, skin, and eyes are extremely common — almost everyone experiences this. You may also notice dry nose, occasional nosebleeds, mild joint or muscle aches, temporary worsening of acne at the start, increased sensitivity to sunlight, and dry or irritated eyes if you wear contact lenses.
warnings: This medication can cause very serious birth defects if taken during pregnancy — it must never be taken if you are pregnant or could become pregnant without using two forms of birth control. All patients must be enrolled in a special safety program called iPLEDGE and have regular check-ins. It can also affect your mood in some people, so let your doctor know right away if you feel depressed or have unusual thoughts. Avoid vitamin A supplements, prolonged sun exposure, and do not donate blood while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on your body weight and is usually taken once or twice daily with a full meal for about 15 to 20 weeks (about 4 to 5 months). Taking it with food — especially something containing fat — helps your body absorb it much better. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how you respond and any side effects you experience.
